name: which-ranking
title: Three rankings from one posterior
idea: One posterior can rank units differently by posterior mean, by expected rank and by the chance of being on top when the posteriors differ in width or shape, and each unit's own rank is uncertain.
from: v1 whole · v1 L-09 which-ranking; adds a scale switch (θ or √θ on the ch. 19 law, θ or exp(kθ) on the league) under which only the posterior-mean ranking moves
credit: Built for this site; the three-unit law after the postrank theory book, ch. 19; expected ranks after ch. 5; the scale switch after ch. 4 and 12; rankings by posterior means after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section IV.B and the notes to Figure 2C, and talk slide 59.
